title: Separating the Components of Quick Ache Relief
description: Test pure-component properties, design and obtain approval for a separation, recover sucrose and acetaminophen while testing for possible aspirin, and evaluate consumer label hypotheses with gravimetric evidence.
audience: Chemistry students completing a guided-inquiry consumer-product separation investigation.
learningGoals: Use experimental property evidence for pure sucrose, acetaminophen, and aspirin to justify a separation design.
Execute a teacher-approved liquid-liquid or acid-base extraction with safe venting, labeled fractions, filtration, drying, and gravimetry.
Calculate component mass percentages and total recovery separately, then evaluate label accuracy and possible aspirin evidence with uncertainty.
Explain the separation at the particulate level using polarity, ion formation, partitioning, precipitation, filtration, and drying.
safetyNotes: Wear safety goggles at all times and review relevant SDS information before selecting tests or a separation.
Treat acid and base solutions as skin and eye burn hazards.
Keep ethyl acetate away from ignition sources and use extreme caution with any approved heating.
Vent the separatory funnel away from people and relieve pressure during mixing.
Place liquid and solid waste only in teacher-designated containers.
